title: Duchy of Mecklenburg
capsule: The Duchy of Mecklenburg designates the brief interlude between 1806 and 1815 when the two longstanding Mecklenburg duchies — Schwerin and Strelitz — joined Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine as ducal states before Napoleon annexed northern Germany in 1810, temporarily dissolving their autonomy. Following Napoleon's defeat, the Congress of Vienna in 1815 restored both territories and elevated them to Grand Duchies of Mecklenburg-Schwerin and Mecklenburg-Strelitz respectively, rewarding their dynasties for switching allegiances to the anti-Napoleonic coalition in 1813. The ruling house descended from the Obotrite prince Niklot and had governed Mecklenburg, with brief interruptions, since the twelfth century. The 1815 elevation ended the duchy period proper and ushered in the grand-ducal era that lasted until 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent during this brief period is well-established from Confederation of the Rhine records and Congress of Vienna documentation.
